plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Exit concentrated AI/Software (METU, PLTU, MSFU) and Semis (MUU) positions.
Reduce Income ETF (QQQI) to 20% to build cash buffer.

conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation, aiming for lower monthly gains around 1.5%. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged ETFs and concentrated positions, building a substantial cash buffer. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to low single digits.

balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% monthly growth while prioritizing risk management. It trims leverage and concentration, adding a new, well-rated stock. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a focus on steady, risk-controlled gains.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 6% each.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for higher monthly growth around 4%, accepting significantly increased risk and potential drawdowns. It leans into leveraged ETFs and concentrated sectors, with a smaller cash buffer. Be aware of amplified volatility and the daily decay of leveraged ETFs.

Increase Income ETF (QQQI) to 30% for steady distributions.
Hold broad index ETFs (SPY, QQQ) for stability.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly distributions, prioritizing capital preservation and steady cash flow. It eliminates leverage and high-beta growth stocks, shifting towards income-generating ETFs like QQQI. Expect low volatility, but NAV can still decline in market downturns.
